content.title: KITCHEN FIXES FOR ANNOYING LITTLE PROBLEMS {{NOBODY TELLS YOU ABOUT}}
facts: **Hiccups** – Swallow a spoonful of sugar; the grainy texture interrupts the nerve spasm causing the spasm loop.
**Stuffy Nose** – Press your tongue to the roof of your mouth and your thumb between your eyebrows for 20 seconds to loosen mucus.
**Burnt Tongue** – Press a spoonful of sugar or honey on the spot for instant numbing relief.
**Leg Cramp** – Pinch your upper lip hard for 20 seconds; it can interrupt the nerve signal causing the muscle spasm.
**Brain Freeze** – Press your tongue flat against the roof of your mouth to warm the area fast.
**Dry, Cracked Heels** – Rub a thick layer of petroleum jelly on feet, then wear socks overnight.
**Smelly Hands After Chopping Onion or Garlic** – Rub your hands on stainless steel (like a spoon) under running water to neutralize the odor.
**Stye On The Eyelid** – Apply a warm, damp washcloth over the closed eye for 10 minutes, 3x/day, to help it drain.
**Minor Kitchen Burn** – Run it under cool (not ice-cold) water for 10 minutes before anything else touches it.
**Restless Hiccuping Baby Or Upset Stomach Feeling** – Sip warm water slowly instead of cold, it relaxes the stomach muscles.
**Follow along** – for more quick, practical fixes like this.

caption:
A few of these are worth understanding, not just memorizing. The sugar trick for hiccups works because the slightly abrasive texture overstimulates the vagus nerve, which helps override the diaphragm spasm causing the hiccup in the first place. The lip pinch for leg cramps works on a similar idea: pain receptors near the lip can distract the nervous system enough to interrupt the misfiring signal telling your calf muscle to seize up. And that stainless steel trick for onion smell isn't folklore either, the sulfur compounds on your skin actually bind to the metal molecules and rinse away with the water, instead of lingering on your hands. Everyone's body is different, so give these a try and see what actually works for you.
